source: R. Elwaradi, J. Mehta, T. H. Ngo, M. Nemoz, C. Bougerol, F. Medjdoub and Y. Cordier, J. Appl. Phys. 133, 145705 (2023), doi:10.1063/5.0147048, Tables I and II and text; read from the author version deposited in HAL (hal-04086494, open access). Values copied without change.
structure_from_text: NH3-MBE on Al-polar bulk AlN substrates (HexaTech, dislocation density below 1e3 cm^-2). AlN buffer, GaN channel of 500 down to 8 nm, then a barrier made of a 1 nm AlN spacer plus a 19 nm AlGaN layer with nominal Al content 30%, capped with a thin GaN layer (cap thickness not given). The 2DEG density was measured by mercury-probe capacitance-voltage or by the Hall effect; the sheet resistance by van der Pauw or eddy current.
text_on_barrier_relaxation: On thin, highly compressed GaN channels the 30% barrier has a larger mismatch with the channel; XRD shows that it 'relaxed approximately 20%-25% of its mismatch strain with GaN'. The authors estimate this mismatch at about 1.7% for the barrier on sub-10 nm channels (in-plane lattice of AlN).
notes: Consistency check: for the 20 nm channel, 1/(e n mu) = 1/(1.602e-19 * 2.2e12 * 310) = 9.2 kOhm/sq, the van der Pauw value of Table II (9000).

On the 20 nm channel (GaN relaxation 8 percent, so its in-plane lattice is close to that of AlN) the 30 percent barrier is under compression, not tension: its relaxation is a misfit network of the opposite sign to that of the Shen and Hiroki series.
